messages:
sara: Heads-up — got a finance alert for a ~$12k/day spike overnight. Looks tied to autoscaler activity in eu-west1.
ben: saw that. graphs show a sudden fan-out at 03:12 UTC to 120 nodes.
anya: curious — those are CPU-only instances, not our GPU pools? :thinking_face:
paul: yep, the launched ones are c6i-large variants, not a100/p4. logs show nodeTemplate.label 'gpu=true' was missing on the new provisioner.
sara: how did autoscaler pick c6i? our config should prefer gpu families. maybe constraint order fell back to cheapest compatible.
ben: here's the relevant snippet from the provisioner created by the new terraform module:
```
nodeSelector:
  gpu: "true"
instanceTypes: ["n1-highmem-8", "c6i-large"]
```
anya: ugh nodeSelector uses string "true" vs boolean, and our selector checks for label presence not value. if label absent, it becomes match-any and picks c6i.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-10T03:10:12Z — autoscaler-policy v2.1 applied to cluster eu-west1-m
finance-bot: Billing alert — daily forecast deviation 780% vs baseline for project redwood-prod-eu-west1
paul: also billing shows these instances were billed as on-demand. we have committed reservations for GPU family tied to reservation-id tag, but the CPU instances don't map so no reservation discount applied.
cloudops: I pulled invoice lines: 120 * c6i.large on-demand for 8 hours = ~11k. Reservation utilization for GPU family remained high but unused credits can't be applied to CPU SKUs.
sara: so two failures: (1) provisioner dropped gpu label -> wrong families launched, (2) reservation tags/filters didn't catch wrong launches so cost saving lost.
ben: temporary mitigation: scale the bad instance group to 0, re-run provisioner with explicit "requireLabel: gpu" and update terraform plan.
anya: can we also add an admission webhook to reject node requests without gpu label when pool type==gpu?
paul: I'm on the scale-down now. running:
```
kubectl scale --replicas=0 nodepool/ephemeral-cpu-spill -n kube-system
```
paul: scaled. autoscaler should stop launching. watching.
sara: finance reached out — ask cloud provider for retroactive credit for misbilled on-demand launches due to our misconfig. finance will open ticket.
finance-bot: Support case created with cloud provider: INC-86214. Attach invoice: gs://billing/2026-03/invoice-eu-west1-03-10.pdf
cloudops: plan to harden: (1) requireLabel in proton/terraform module, (2) admission webhook, (3) alert when autoscaler launches non-gpu instances while gpu reservation utilization > 60%, (4) pre-deploy lint that checks nodeSelector + instanceTypes overlap.
anya: I'll draft the admission webhook PR and add unit tests.
ben: I'll update the terraform module and add the preflight check to CICD lint job.
sara: Paul, please follow up on support ticket and share any SLA/credits notes when cloud responds.
paul: noted, I'll ping finance and update thread.
cloudops: tagging for postmortem: autoscaler-config, terraform-module, billing, reservations
sara: thanks team. let's do a quick retro after we have the credits outcome. :thumbsup:
